study.title: Exploring the changes in functional connectivity of the limbic system in Patients with amnestic mild cognitive impairment treated by acupuncture based on fMRI
study.study_design: Non-randomized controlled trial with pre-post design and healthy control comparison group
study.randomization: non-randomized controlled method was employed for grouping
study.population: patients with amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) aged 55-75 years and healthy participants aged 55-75 years
study.inclusion_criteria: aMCI: (1) Aged between 55 and 75 years old; (2) Selection of individuals without bad habits, such as non-smoking and non-alcoholism; (3) Self-reported or reported by others to have mild memory problems; (4) MMSE scoring criteria: for the illiterate group, the score is >= 17 points; for the primary school education group, the score is >= 20 points; for the group with junior high school education or above, the score is >= 24 points. In the tests of memory or other cognitive domains, the performance is lower than that of peers but higher than 1.5 standard deviations below the standard score, and the score of the Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) scale is 0.5 points; (5) The total score of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scale is <= 26 points, and other diseases that can cause cognitive impairment, such as brain trauma, stroke, Parkinson's disease, and hypothyroidism, are excluded; (6) The results of cranial MRI examination are normal, and the skin at the acupuncture site is intact without scars; (7) Before the experiment, the individuals have not received acupuncture treatment in the past two months and have no physical discomfort. HC: (1) No obvious behavioral and language disorders; (2) Normal cognitive function assessment; (3) Right-handed; (4) No neurological diseases, etc.
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) Obvious dementia; (2) Having impairments such as visual, auditory, or aphasic disorders, or other severe cognitive impairments, such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, etc.; (3) Suffering from major mental illnesses or severe visceral dysfunctional diseases of the heart, liver, kidneys, etc.; (4) Long-term use of drugs that affect cognitive abilities, such as benzodiazepines, anticholinergic drugs, etc.; or those who have taken sedative drugs within the last month before the trial; or having diseases that may affect cognitive performance, such as epilepsy, brain tumors, severe head trauma, etc.; (5) Drug abuse or alcoholism; (6) Having a pacemaker or metal fragments in the body that affect magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanning; (7) Having psychological diseases such as claustrophobia and being unable to undergo MRI scanning; (8) Congenital cranial malformation; (9) Color blindness, etc.

interventions.needle_type_exact: disposable Huatuo-brand stainless steel flat-handle acupuncture needle
interventions.manipulation_exact: reinforcing-reducing manipulation was applied, needle twirling was carried out. Duration of needle twirling was 60 s. Twirling angle was controlled within the range of 180° ± 20°, and the frequency was 60–90 times per minute
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: subject would experience the deqi sensations such as soreness, numbness, distension, and heaviness. After achieving deqi, the needle was retained for 40 min
interventions.session_duration_exact: needling every 10 min, retaining the needles for 40 min
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: once a day, 6 days of treatment + 1 day of rest, 4 weeks as one course, starting the second course after an interval of 2 weeks; two courses of treatment
interventions.treatment_period_exact: two courses of treatment (4 weeks as one course, starting the second course after an interval of 2 weeks)
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: acupuncturist who has more than 10 years of professional experience
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: based on the theory of host-guest Yuanluo point pairing, this technique has been widely applied in the field of cognitive impairment with significant efficacy

non_acupoint_locations_exact: all non-meridian and non-acupoints, located 0.5 cun away from the actual acupoints to be needled, bypassing the acupoints
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: 0.5 cun away from the actual acupoints to be needled, bypassing the acupoints
interventions.manipulation_exact: acupuncture intervention measures and the protocol are all consistent with those of the true-acupoint group

interventions.treatment_period_exact: same as true-acupoint group: two courses of treatment

interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: to rule out the brain effects caused by the pain of acupuncture, so as to accurately evaluate the effect of acupuncture at the acupoints

extraction_notes.note: Deqi/sensory response was described narratively as intended ('soreness, numbness, distension, and heaviness') but no quantitative deqi scale (e.g., MASS, PAS) was administered or reported. No deqi scores are available for extraction.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported. The paper makes no mention of expectancy scales, credibility measures, or participant guessing of allocation.
Adverse events were not reported. The paper does not include a dedicated adverse events section.
Trial registration number is not reported in the paper.

The sham acupuncture procedure description states location is '0.5 cun away from the actual acupoints to be needled, bypassing the acupoints' but does not specify needle penetration depth, whether needles penetrated skin, or manipulation performed at sham locations. This is a critical limitation for classifying the sham type.

The table thresholding note states 'The initial voxel-level threshold was set at p = 0.000 (FWEc corrected)' but this is likely a reporting artifact (p-value cannot equal exactly 0.000). The methods section states 'voxel-level p = 0.001 (uncorrected) and cluster-level p < 0.05 (FWEc corrected)'. There is an apparent inconsistency between the methods description and the table footnotes.

Table 5 (true-acupoint post vs HC) contains many seeds (Seed1 through Seed30) but Table 7 (true-acupoint pre vs post within-group) also has extensive results. Due to the large volume of coordinate rows, not all rows from Table 5 extended content were individually verified. The most salient rows were extracted; some additional rows in the extensive Table 5 (Seeds 10-30) may require supplemental verification.

The paper reports inter-group comparison between true-acupoint pre and sham-acupoint pre groups showing only Seed10, Seed12, and Seed17 passed FWEc correction but with extremely small voxel counts making graphical presentation impossible. No coordinates are reported for this comparison.

The paper reports that after-acupuncture inter-group comparison between true and sham groups showed Seed2, Seed10, Seed11, Seed12, Seed14, Seed19, Seed24, Seed25 passed FWEc correction but with extremely small voxel counts. No coordinates are provided for this comparison.

The paper states n=50 aMCI patients were recruited, with 35 in true-acupoint and 15 in sham-acupoint groups. The neuropsychological comparison table shows 41 HC, 35 aMCI true-acupoint, 15 aMCI sham-acupoint, totaling 91. This is consistent with the stated total of 91 subjects.

FOV is reported as '220 mm × 220 mm × 143 mm' in image acquisition, but voxel size is only partially described via matrix (64×64), slices (36), thickness (3mm), gap (1mm). Explicit voxel dimensions (e.g., 3.4×3.4×3 mm) are not stated directly.

Table 7 row for Seed18 Cingulum_Post_R shows brain region cell blank in the PDF text extraction (coordinates 3, -63, 45 with T=-6.0879 but region name is missing). This appears to be an OCR/table formatting issue.

The paper mentions correlations between FC and neuropsychological scales but does not report post-acupuncture correlations comprehensively - only states 'there were few indicators showing a significant correlation'. Only two scatter plot results are shown for the true-acupoint post group and two for the sham-acupoint post group in Figures 12 and 13.
Smoothing kernel size (FWHM) is not explicitly reported, only that spatial smoothing was performed.
CDR scale was mentioned in inclusion criteria but no CDR scores are reported in demographic or outcome tables.

Due to the very large number of rows in Table 5 (true-acupoint post vs HC), not every single row could be individually included as a coordinate entry without causing extreme JSON length. Key representative rows and all rows from Table 3, 4, 7, 8 have been included. The full Table 5 contains additional rows for Seeds not individually listed here that would require further human verification.
